title: At Nasdaq opening bell, Anthropic CEO recommits to pacing AI development
lede: Before the Nasdaq opening bell on Anthropic's first trading day, Dario Amodei pledged to pace AI training and deployment until the company is confident its systems are safe and stay under human control.

points: Amodei opened with his father's death from a disease that became curable a few years later, and argued AI working with scientists could compress a century of medical progress into a decade.
He listed the risks as misuse by individuals or states, economic disruption and loss of control, calling them avoidable rather than inevitable.
He said Anthropic will not bend to business or political pressure, and that going public strengthens that resolve.
More of the company's talent will go to checking that its systems are safe, he said, with the hardest safety work still ahead.
He restated the race to the top: proving safety and commercial success can coexist so that rivals follow.

sections.text: A pledge to slow training and deployment, made on listing day, is now a public commitment that shareholders and customers can hold Anthropic to as it ships new models.
